The margin comment accurately describes the change and available fallbacks.

f-insurance-51b7033b.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred insurance position: CGL at USD 1M per occurrence/2M aggregate, E&O at USD 2M, cyber at USD 5M when Garman handles Sparkling data, statutory workers’ compensation, and certificates on request. It preserves the existing headings provision and is professionally drafted. However, requiring all coverage to continue for one year after termination exceeds the stated playbook and is not necessary, particularly for CGL and workers’ compensation, so the redline is not strictly minimal.

f-license-126cf1e0.reason: The redline appropriately extends use to contractors acting on Sparkling’s behalf and permits transfer in an M&A transaction, but it omits the required perpetual and irrevocable treatment for paid-up licences and the uncured-material-breach termination limitation for subscription licences. It also unnecessarily gives Garman a reciprocal no-consent assignment right, changing supplier-side commercial rights beyond what the playbook requires. Further, the licence remains described as “non-transferable” without an express qualification in the grant itself, creating avoidable tension with Section 20(d).

f-lol-cap-6aa14499.reason: The clause meets the fallback position: the cap and consequential-damages exclusion are mutual, the cap is at least as protective as 12 months' fees, and the required fallback carve-outs are included, assuming Section 14 is confidentiality. It also addresses payment obligations appropriately. It does not fully reach the preferred position because data protection and security breaches are not expressly carved out, and the fee lookback runs from the event giving rise to the claim rather than the claim itself. The drafting is otherwise focused and professional.

f-nosolicit-21ea7cc0.reason: The clause appropriately converts the no-hire into a mutual non-solicit, limits it to directly involved personnel, and includes the required general-recruitment and unsolicited-approach carve-outs. However, the restriction applies “during the term” as well as for 12 months after an individual’s involvement ends. If involvement ends before the Agreement terminates, this could extend the restriction beyond 12 months from that individual’s involvement, contrary to the fallback. It should instead apply during the individual’s involvement and for 12 months thereafter.

f-transition-021e6973.reason: The added clause reaches the preferred position: up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, data return within 30 days in a commonly used machine-readable format, and certified deletion thereafter. It preserves the existing termination and perpetual-license provisions. However, it is not strictly minimal because it extends the return and deletion obligations beyond Customer Data to all Sparkling Confidential Information, and applying a machine-readable-format requirement to all Confidential Information may be overbroad or impractical. Otherwise, the operative language is professionally drafted.

f-audit-eaf8650a.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: one audit per twelve months, thirty days’ written notice, business-hours review, an independent auditor subject to written confidentiality obligations, Vendor-paid costs unless underpayment exceeds 5%, and no system access. The revision is narrowly focused and preserves the remaining audit protections. However, it is not strictly minimal because Section 22.1 prohibits all access to Customer systems, while the playbook and existing Section 22.2 require only that there be no direct access. That broader and duplicative formulation should instead track Section 22.2 by stating that Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly.

f-exclusivity-d350eef7.reason: Deleting Section 2.2 fully achieves the preferred position by removing the sole-supplier obligation. Because the original clause addressed only exclusivity, full deletion is the narrowest effective change and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms. The margin comment accurately describes the deletion and appropriately identifies the fallback without attempting to substitute commentary for operative language.

f-ld-e4497af0.reason: The redline reaches the preferred position by eliminating all liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer. Replacing the per-day charge with an equitable schedule extension appropriately preserves Vendor relief for Customer-caused delay without introducing a monetary remedy. The change is targeted and professionally drafted, though “obligations shall be extended” is slightly imprecise; “deadlines for affected obligations” would be clearer.

f-mfn-b005cd8a.reason: Deleting Section 7.2 fully achieves the preferred position of imposing no MFN obligation on Customer. The change is limited to the offending obligation, does not affect any separate MFN pricing protection benefiting Customer, and requires no replacement language.

f-nosolicit-0d12d799.reason: Deleting § 12.4 fully achieves the preferred position of no employee non-solicitation restriction on Customer. Because the entire clause consists solely of the disfavored restriction, full deletion is necessary and does not alter unrelated commercial terms. The margin comment accurately describes the preferred and fallback positions.

f-renewal-81304192.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: automatic renewals remain limited to 12 months, Customer may opt out on 30 days’ written notice, Vendor must provide a reminder at least 60 days before renewal, and renewal increases remain capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%. The revisions are limited to the renewal mechanics, preserve the original bilateral non-renewal right and unrelated fee provisions, and are professionally drafted.

f-govlaw-4a18e833.reason: The operative language adopts the preferred New York governing law and exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County. The revision is limited to replacing the conflicting Singapore-law provision and appropriately cross-referencing the existing forum clause. It preserves the existing jurisdiction submission, venue and forum-non-conveniens waivers, and temporary-injunctive-relief carveout, and is professionally drafted.

f-indemn-4b4a32cd.reason: The operative language substantively reaches the preferred position: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates for third-party IP, legal-compliance, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, and gross-negligence/wilful-misconduct claims; it includes standard procedures and narrowly limits Customer's indemnity. The IP exclusions and remedies are customary and consistent with the fallback, while unrelated terms remain unchanged. Drafting quality is reduced because the inserted provisions are not numbered even though they refer to Sections 20.1(a) and 20.5, leaving broken or ambiguous cross-references. The margin comment also cites Sections 19.4 and 30.5 inconsistently with the supplied text.

f-ip-4d5f6eab.reason: The clause appropriately gives Customer exclusive ownership of Deliverables, includes a present assignment, and excludes Vendor's pre-existing technology. However, it does not establish Customer's ownership of Customer Data. It also relies on an unseen Section 13.2 for the embedded Vendor IP licence, so the required perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence cannot be confirmed from the operative language provided. The changes are otherwise targeted and professionally drafted.

f-mfn-8543a675.reason: Deleting Section 7.2 fully achieves the preferred position of imposing no MFN obligation on Customer. Because the entire clause consists of the prohibited disclosure-and-matching obligation, full deletion is necessary and does not disturb unrelated commercial terms. The margin comment accurately explains the deletion, and the operative result is clear.

f-mincommit-b4ab0b09.reason: The revision achieves the preferred position by eliminating the three-year minimum and take-or-pay obligation and limiting payment obligations to Services actually used or ordered under an executed Order Form. It leaves the unrelated protections in Section 12.3 unchanged, aligns with that section’s existing no-minimum-volume language, and is clear and professionally drafted.

f-noncompete-00a4a55e.reason: The redline fully achieves the preferred position by deleting the non-compete and retaining § 12.3’s express confirmation that Customer has no non-compete, exclusivity, or field-of-use restriction. The change is limited to the offending provision, preserves unrelated commercial terms, and is professionally drafted. The margin comment accurately explains the deletion and appropriately identifies the fallback without introducing it into the operative language.

f-nosolicit-b5a8fdcb.reason: The clause otherwise tracks the fallback: it is mutual, limited to employees directly involved in the Services, excludes hiring restrictions, and includes carve-outs for general recruitment and unsolicited approaches. However, “During the term and for twelve months after the end of an individual's involvement” can restrict solicitation throughout the entire contract term even where the individual's involvement ended more than 12 months earlier. The restriction should instead apply during the individual's involvement and for 12 months thereafter, or otherwise expire 12 months after that involvement ends. The redline is otherwise targeted and professionally drafted.

f-t4c-d6e38846.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: Customer receives a 30-day convenience-termination right, a refund of prepaid fees attributable to the post-termination period, and Vendor has no convenience-termination right during a term. However, allowing termination of the Agreement or an Order Form “in whole or in part” goes beyond the stated playbook requirement and is ambiguous as to whether Customer may selectively terminate contractual obligations or service components, potentially disrupting unrelated pricing and scope arrangements. Deleting “in whole or in part” would make the revision more targeted and precise.

f-transition-c3240419.reason: The addition appropriately provides up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates and requires machine-readable data export followed by deletion certification. However, the 30-day export deadline runs from Customer’s request rather than from expiry or termination, so Vendor has no automatic obligation to return the data within 30 days of the triggering event as required by both the preferred and fallback positions. Otherwise, the change is targeted, preserves the existing commercial terms, and is professionally drafted.

f-exclusivity-75577550.reason: The operative language fully reaches the preferred position by removing Customer’s sole-supplier obligation and expressly preserving Customer’s right to use third-party providers. It makes only targeted changes to Section 2.2, leaves the broader protections in Section 12.3 intact, and preserves the underlying commercial intent that Vendor will provide hosted analytics services. The added minimum-volume clarification is consistent with Section 12.3 and does not introduce an unrelated change. The drafting is clear and professional.

f-indemn-af20a8b9.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: it narrows Customer’s indemnity to Customer-provided materials and breach of law, and adds Vendor indemnities for third-party IP claims, breach of law, Vendor-caused unauthorized access or disclosure, and gross negligence or wilful misconduct. It also includes standard notice, defence control, settlement, participation, and cooperation procedures. The IP exclusions and remedies are consistent with the fallback and remain confined to the indemnity framework. The principal drafting defect is the reference to “Section 20.2(a),” because the added Vendor indemnity is not numbered as Section 20.2; the new paragraphs should be numbered and cross-references conformed.

f-license-8dd04f65.reason: The redline minimally and appropriately extends the Services licence to Affiliates and contractors, restricts revocation of subscription rights to specified uncured material breaches, and permits successor transfers. However, Section 13.3 applies its revocation exception to “a licence” without carving out the perpetual, irrevocable paid-up licences in Section 13.2. That creates a material conflict with the required absolute irrevocability of paid-up licences. Section 13.3 should expressly apply only to subscription licences, or expressly exclude licences granted under Section 13.2. The phrase “except during a material uncured…breach” is also less precise than stating that termination or suspension may occur only after notice and failure to cure.

f-lol-cap-48c632ad.reason: The redline appropriately makes the cap mutual and raises it to the preferred greater-of threshold without altering unrelated commercial terms. However, the supplied operative language does not define “Excluded Claims,” establish the required carve-outs, provide a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, or clarify that Customer payment obligations are not damages. The margin comment cannot substitute for operative language or verify provisions in Sections 21.2 and 21.3. Accordingly, the preferred position—and, absent an operative definition of Excluded Claims, even the fallback carve-outs—is not established by the text provided.

f-mincommit-953097f3.reason: The operative language fully reaches the preferred position by eliminating the minimum purchase and take-or-pay obligations and limiting Fees to ordered or actually used Services. The revision is confined to the commitment provision, preserves the underlying usage/order-based fee model, and is clear and professionally drafted.

f-noncompete-768576ee.reason: Deleting §12.4 fully achieves the preferred position of no non-compete or field-of-use restriction, while retaining §12.3’s express confirmation of Customer’s freedom to compete. The edit is limited to the offending restriction, preserves unrelated terms, and is professionally drafted. The margin comment accurately explains the deletion and identifies the fallback position.

f-transition-3e7ce3f7.reason: The operative language reaches the preferred position: transition assistance is available on expiry or termination for up to six months at then-current rates; Customer Data must be returned within 30 days of request in a complete, commonly used, machine-readable format; and remaining data must then be securely deleted with written officer certification. The revision appropriately replaces only the contradictory immediate-cessation and deletion language in Section 11.1 while preserving the more protective existing provisions in Sections 11.2 and 11.3. The drafting is clear, internally consistent, and professional.

f-warranty-544c9b8a.reason: The redline improves the Deliverable conformity period to the 90-day fallback and preserves the repair, replacement, re-performance, and refund remedies. However, it does not add the required compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranties, and it does not clearly establish the required warranty period for Services. Moreover, Section 19.1 contains an apparently unlimited Deliverable conformity warranty while Section 19.2 provides a 90-day period and expressly does not limit Section 19.1, creating avoidable ambiguity. The changes are otherwise narrow and preserve unrelated commercial terms.

f-ld-7a202273.reason: The redline reaches the preferred position by eliminating liquidated damages and penalties. However, it goes beyond what is necessary by extending the delinquency period from 10 to 30 days, adding “proper, undisputed” invoice qualifications, and making interest Vendor’s “sole remedy,” which could unintentionally eliminate suspension, termination, collection-cost, or other contractual remedies. The interest provision is otherwise professionally drafted, but “sole remedy” should be limited to the monetary consequence of late payment or omitted.

f-lol-cap-4f2ba9d3.reason: The revised cap is mutual and matches the preferred monetary formulation while narrowly correcting the restrictive Fees definition. However, the operative language supplied does not establish the required Excluded Claims; the margin comment cannot substitute for an operative definition. It also does not provide the preferred mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, the IP-infringement carve-out, or clarification that Customer payment obligations are not damages. Without operative confirmation of at least the fallback carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, and wilful misconduct, compliance with even the fallback is not demonstrated.
